questions.text:
The output of a 2-input multiplexer is connected back to one of its inputs as shown in the figure.

Match the functional equivalence of this circuit to one of the following options.
questions.solution:
The output Q is fed back to input 0.
- S = 1: Q follows input 1 (the data input D).
- S = 0: Q = Q, so it holds its old value.

It is transparent while S = 1 and holds while S = 0, which is a level-triggered D latch (S acts as enable). There is no clock edge, so it is not a flip-flop.

Answer: D Latch

questions.text:
Which one or more of the following need to be saved on a context switch from one
thread (T1) of a process to another thread (T2) of the same process?
questions.solution:
Threads of the same process share the address space, so the page table base register does not change and need not be saved.

Each thread has its own execution context: stack pointer, program counter and general purpose registers [latex]\text{---}[/latex] these must be saved.

Answer: Stack pointer, Program counter, General purpose registers

questions.text:
Which one or more of the following options guarantee that a computer system will
transition from user mode to kernel mode?
questions.solution:
Check which events always enter the kernel:
- Function call: runs entirely in user mode [latex]\text{---}[/latex] no switch.
- malloc: a library function; it usually takes memory from the existing heap and makes a system call only sometimes [latex]\text{---}[/latex] not guaranteed.
- Page fault: an exception handled by the OS [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always kernel mode.
- System call: a trap into the kernel [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] always kernel mode.

Answer: Page Fault, System Call

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are CORRECT?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Regular languages are closed under intersection [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- CFLs are not closed under intersection: [latex]a^nb^nc^m\cap a^mb^nc^n=a^nb^nc^n[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Recursive: run both deciders, accept if both accept [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- RE: run both recognizers, accept when both accept [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 1, 3 and 4

options: The intersection of two regular languages is regular.
The intersection of two context-free languages is context-free.
The intersection of two recursive languages is recursive.
The intersection of two recursively enumerable languages is recursively enumerable.

questions.text:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT about
the OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocol used in the Internet?
questions.solution:
OSPF is a link-state protocol.
- "Implements Bellman-Ford": it uses Dijkstra (Bellman-Ford is for distance vector, like RIP) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] INCORRECT.
- "Uses Dijkstra" [latex]\text{---}[/latex] correct.
- "Inter-domain protocol": OSPF is intra-domain (inside one AS); BGP is inter-domain [latex]\text{---}[/latex] INCORRECT.
- "Hierarchical routing" with areas and a backbone [latex]\text{---}[/latex] correct.

Answer: Options 1 and 3

options: OSPF implements Bellman-Ford algorithm to find shortest paths.
OSPF uses Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm to implement least-cost path routing
OSPF is used as an inter-domain routing protocol
